chapterTitle: The Earthly Tent and the Blood of Christ
themeTitle: “Through His Own Blood, Once for All”

scripture.text: Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service, and an earthly sanctuary.
scripture.understanding: εἶχε μὲν οὖν καὶ ἡ πρώτη δικαιώματα λατρείας, “Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service” — δικαίωμα, a regulation; λατρεία, worship (related to λατρεύω in the servant family). τό τε ἅγιον κοσμικόν, “and an earthly sanctuary” — κοσμικός, of this world (κόσμος, world family). The old covenant was not worthless; it had God-given worship and a God-given sanctuary. But it was ‘of this world’.

scripture.text: For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread; which is called the Holy Place.
scripture.understanding: σκηνὴ γὰρ κατεσκευάσθη ἡ πρώτη, “For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part” — the outer room. ἐν ᾗ ἥ τε λυχνία καὶ ἡ τράπεζα καὶ ἡ πρόθεσις τῶν ἄρτων, “were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread” — literally ‘the setting-forth of the loaves’: twelve loaves set before God each Sabbath. ἥτις λέγεται ἅγια, “which is called the Holy Place.”

scripture.text: After the second veil was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies,
scripture.understanding: μετὰ δὲ τὸ δεύτερον καταπέτασμα, “After the second veil” — the inner curtain, the one torn at Jesus' death. σκηνὴ ἡ λεγομένη ἅγια ἁγίων, “was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies” — the Most Holy Place, where God's presence dwelt above the ark.

scripture.text: having a golden altar of incense, and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;
scripture.understanding: χρυσοῦν ἔχουσα θυμιατήριον, “having a golden altar of incense” — the incense altar actually stood just outside the veil, but it belonged closely to the inner room, since its incense was carried inside on the Day of Atonement; some translate the word ‘censer’. καὶ τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης περικεκαλυμμένην πάντοθεν χρυσίῳ, “and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold.” Inside: στάμνος χρυσῆ ἔχουσα τὸ μάννα, “a golden pot holding the manna” — God's provision; ἡ ῥάβδος Ἀαρὼν ἡ βλαστήσασα, “Aaron’s rod that budded” — God's chosen priesthood; καὶ αἱ πλάκες τῆς διαθήκης, “and the tablets of the covenant” — God's law.

scripture.text: and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which things we can’t speak now in detail.
scripture.understanding: ὑπεράνω δὲ αὐτῆς Χερουβὶν δόξης κατασκιάζοντα τὸ ἱλαστήριον, “and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat.” ἱλαστήριον, the place of atonement, the golden lid of the ark where blood was sprinkled — the same word Paul uses of Christ in Romans 3:25. περὶ ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν νῦν λέγειν κατὰ μέρος, “of which things we can’t speak now in detail” — the writer could say much more, but his point is elsewhere.

scripture.text: Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services,
scripture.understanding: τούτων δὲ οὕτως κατεσκευασμένων, “Now these things having been thus prepared,” εἰς μὲν τὴν πρώτην σκηνὴν διὰ παντὸς εἰσίασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὰς λατρείας ἐπιτελοῦντες, “the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services” — trimming lamps, burning incense, changing the bread. Daily, endless activity.

scripture.text: but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself, and for the errors of the people.
scripture.understanding: εἰς δὲ τὴν δευτέραν ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ μόνος ὁ ἀρχιερεύς, “but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year” — on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16). οὐ χωρὶς αἵματος, “not without blood,” ὃ προσφέρει ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ ἀγνοημάτων, “which he offers for himself, and for the errors of the people.” ἀγνόημα, added to the sin family: sins of ignorance, wrongs done without full knowledge. One man, one day a year, with blood: access to God was severely restricted.

scripture.text: The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing;
scripture.understanding: τοῦτο δηλοῦντος τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, “The Holy Spirit is indicating this” — the Spirit was teaching through the very layout of the tabernacle. μήπω πεφανερῶσθαι τὴν τῶν ἁγίων ὁδόν, “that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed” — φανερόω from the appear family. ἔτι τῆς πρώτης σκηνῆς ἐχούσης στάσιν, “while the first tabernacle was still standing.” The curtain itself preached a sermon: ‘Not yet. The way is not open.’

scripture.text: which is a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect;
scripture.understanding: ἥτις παραβολὴ εἰς τὸν καιρὸν τὸν ἐνεστηκότα, “which is a symbol of the present age” — παραβολή from the pattern family: a picture set alongside. A word-family point: ‘age’ here is καιρός, the time family's word for a season with a particular character — not αἰών, the word for the ages in verse 26. καθ᾽ ἣν δῶρά τε καὶ θυσίαι προσφέρονται, “where gifts and sacrifices are offered” — the offering family again. μὴ δυνάμεναι κατὰ συνείδησιν τελειῶσαι τὸν λατρεύοντα, “that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect” — τελειόω from the perfect family. They could cleanse the body ritually but could not reach the conscience.

scripture.text: being only (with meats and drinks and various washings) fleshly ordinances, imposed until a time of reformation.
scripture.understanding: μόνον ἐπὶ βρώμασιν καὶ πόμασιν καὶ διαφόροις βαπτισμοῖς, “being only (with meats and drinks and various washings)” — βαπτισμός, ritual washings (as in 6:2). δικαιώματα σαρκός, “fleshly ordinances” — rules for the body. μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως ἐπικείμενα, “imposed until a time of reformation” — καιρός again: the appointed season of διόρθωσις, setting things straight. That season arrived with Christ.

scripture.text: But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation,
scripture.understanding: Χριστὸς δὲ παραγενόμενος ἀρχιερεὺς τῶν γενομένων ἀγαθῶν, “But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things” — ἀγαθός from the good family (some manuscripts read ‘the good things that have come’). διὰ τῆς μείζονος καὶ τελειοτέρας σκηνῆς, “through the greater and more perfect tabernacle” — τέλειος from the perfect family. οὐ χειροποιήτου, τοῦτ᾽ ἔστιν οὐ ταύτης τῆς κτίσεως, “not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation.”

scripture.text: nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.
scripture.understanding: οὐδὲ δι᾽ αἵματος τράγων καὶ μόσχων, “nor yet through the blood of goats and calves,” διὰ δὲ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος, “but through his own blood” — the decisive difference. εἰσῆλθεν ἐφάπαξ εἰς τὰ ἅγια, “entered in once for all into the Holy Place” — ἐφάπαξ, once for all, never to be repeated. αἰωνίαν λύτρωσιν εὑράμενος, “having obtained eternal redemption” — λύτρωσις, release by ransom; αἰώνιος, eternal. The old high priest's work lasted a year; Christ's lasts forever.

scripture.text: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh:
scripture.understanding: εἰ γὰρ τὸ αἷμα τράγων καὶ ταύρων, “For if the blood of goats and bulls” — the Day of Atonement — καὶ σποδὸς δαμάλεως ῥαντίζουσα τοὺς κεκοινωμένους, “and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled” — the red heifer of Numbers 19, whose ashes mixed with water cleansed those defiled by contact with death. ἁγιάζει πρὸς τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς καθαρότητα, “sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh” — they made people ritually clean on the outside.

scripture.text: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
scripture.understanding: πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, “how much more will the blood of Christ,” ὃς διὰ πνεύματος αἰωνίου ἑαυτὸν προσήνεγκεν ἄμωμον τῷ θεῷ, “who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God” — Father, Son and Spirit together in the sacrifice. ἄμωμος, unblemished, the word for a perfect sacrificial animal. καθαριεῖ τὴν συνείδησιν ἡμῶν ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἔργων, “cleanse your conscience from dead works” — what animal blood could never reach. ἔργον from the work family: dead works are deeds that lead to death or religious acts that cannot give life. εἰς τὸ λατρεύειν θεῷ ζῶντι, “to serve the living God” — λατρεύω from the servant family. Cleansed in order to worship.

scripture.text: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant, that those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
scripture.understanding: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο διαθήκης καινῆς μεσίτης ἐστίν, “For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant” — καινός from the new family. ὅπως θανάτου γενομένου εἰς ἀπολύτρωσιν τῶν ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ διαθήκῃ παραβάσεων, “since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant” — παράβασις from the sin family: stepping over God's line. Christ's death reached back to cover the sins of believers under the old covenant too. τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν λάβωσιν οἱ κεκλημένοι τῆς αἰωνίου κληρονομίας, “that those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.”

scripture.text: For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.
scripture.understanding: Now the writer plays on the double meaning of διαθήκη: ‘covenant’ and also, in everyday Greek, ‘will’ or ‘testament’. ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη, “For where a last will and testament is,” θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τοῦ διαθεμένου, “there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.” Some translators keep ‘covenant’ here and understand the death as that of the sacrificial animals by which covenants were ratified; the WEB follows the majority in reading ‘will’. Either way, the point is the same: the new covenant comes into effect through Christ's death.

scripture.text: For a will is in force where there has been death, for it is never in force while he who made it lives.
scripture.understanding: διαθήκη γὰρ ἐπὶ νεκροῖς βεβαία, “For a will is in force where there has been death” — βέβαιος, valid, binding. ἐπεὶ μήποτε ἰσχύει ὅτε ζῇ ὁ διαθέμενος, “for it is never in force while he who made it lives.” An inheritance is received only when the testator dies. Christ died so that His people could receive the ‘eternal inheritance’ (v. 15).

scripture.text: Therefore even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood.
scripture.understanding: ὅθεν οὐδὲ ἡ πρώτη χωρὶς αἵματος ἐγκεκαίνισται, “Therefore even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood” — ἐγκαινίζω, to inaugurate, to put into effect (related to καινός, new). Death and blood stood at the beginning of the old covenant too.

scripture.text: For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
scripture.understanding: λαληθείσης γὰρ πάσης ἐντολῆς κατὰ νόμον ὑπὸ Μωϋσέως παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, “For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law” — at Sinai (Exodus 24). λαβὼν τὸ αἷμα τῶν μόσχων καὶ τῶν τράγων, “he took the blood of the calves and the goats,” μετὰ ὕδατος καὶ ἐρίου κοκκίνου καὶ ὑσσώπου, “with water and scarlet wool and hyssop,” αὐτό τε τὸ βιβλίον καὶ πάντα τὸν λαὸν ἐράντισεν, “and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people.” The covenant was sealed with blood on both the word and the people.

scripture.text: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.”
scripture.understanding: λέγων, “saying,” “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.” Jesus echoed these words at the Last Supper: ‘This is my blood of the new covenant.’ Moses' words pointed forward to Christ's.

scripture.text: Moreover he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν δὲ καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη τῆς λειτουργίας τῷ αἵματι ὁμοίως ἐράντισεν, “Moreover he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.” λειτουργία, priestly service. Everything connected with approaching God had to be cleansed by blood.

scripture.text: According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.
scripture.understanding: καὶ σχεδὸν ἐν αἵματι πάντα καθαρίζεται κατὰ τὸν νόμον, “According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood” — ‘nearly’, because some things were cleansed with water or fire. καὶ χωρὶς αἱματεκχυσίας οὐ γίνεται ἄφεσις, “and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.” αἱματεκχυσία, the pouring out of blood — a word perhaps coined here. ἄφεσις, release, forgiveness. Sin is a matter of life and death; it is forgiven only through a life given.

scripture.text: It was necessary therefore that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
scripture.understanding: ἀνάγκη οὖν τὰ μὲν ὑποδείγματα τῶν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς τούτοις καθαρίζεσθαι, “It was necessary therefore that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these” — ὑπόδειγμα from the pattern family. αὐτὰ δὲ τὰ ἐπουράνια κρείττοσιν θυσίαις παρὰ ταύτας, “but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these” — κρείττων, ‘better’; the plural ‘sacrifices’ refers to the one sacrifice of Christ in its fullness. Why would heavenly things need cleansing? Perhaps because the way to God's presence had to be opened for sinners; the writer does not explain further.

scripture.text: For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands, which are representations of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;
scripture.understanding: οὐ γὰρ εἰς χειροποίητα ἅγια εἰσῆλθεν Χριστός, “For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands,” ἀντίτυπα τῶν ἀληθινῶν, “which are representations of the true” — ἀντίτυπον from the pattern family: counterparts of the real. ἀλλ᾽ εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν οὐρανόν, “but into heaven itself,” νῦν ἐμφανισθῆναι τῷ προσώπῳ τοῦ θεοῦ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, “now to appear in the presence of God for us.” ἐμφανίζω, added to the appear family: to show oneself openly before someone. This is the first of three ‘appearings’ in verses 24–28 — His present appearing before God for us.

scripture.text: nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own,
scripture.understanding: οὐδ᾽ ἵνα πολλάκις προσφέρῃ ἑαυτόν, “nor yet that he should offer himself often,” ὥσπερ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰσέρχεται εἰς τὰ ἅγια κατ᾽ ἐνιαυτὸν ἐν αἵματι ἀλλοτρίῳ, “as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own.” ἀλλότριος, belonging to another — the animal's, not his own.

scripture.text: or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
scripture.understanding: ἐπεὶ ἔδει αὐτὸν πολλάκις παθεῖν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, “or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world” — κόσμος from the world family. νυνὶ δὲ ἅπαξ ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων, “But now once at the end of the ages” — αἰών from the time family: the climax of all history (compare καιρός, ‘the present age’, in v. 9). εἰς ἀθέτησιν ἁμαρτίας διὰ τῆς θυσίας αὐτοῦ πεφανέρωται, “he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.” φανερόω from the appear family: the second ‘appearing’ — His past appearing in history, at the cross. ἀθέτησις, cancellation (as in 7:18): sin set aside, annulled.

scripture.text: Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment,
scripture.understanding: καὶ καθ᾽ ὅσον ἀπόκειται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἅπαξ ἀποθανεῖν, “Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once” — ἀπόκειμαι, laid up, reserved (the same word as the ‘crown laid up’ in 2 Timothy 4:8). μετὰ δὲ τοῦτο κρίσις, “and after this, judgment.” One life, one death, then judgement — no second chances after death, no cycle of rebirth.

scripture.text: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, without sin, to those who are eagerly waiting for him for salvation.
scripture.understanding: οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἅπαξ προσενεχθεὶς εἰς τὸ πολλῶν ἀνενεγκεῖν ἁμαρτίας, “so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many” — ἀναφέρω from the offering family, echoing Isaiah 53: ‘he bore the sin of many’. As humans die once, Christ died once. ἐκ δευτέρου χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας ὀφθήσεται, “will appear a second time, without sin” — ὤφθη, from ὁράω in the appear family: the third ‘appearing’, His future return, not to deal with sin again but to complete salvation. τοῖς αὐτὸν ἀπεκδεχομένοις εἰς σωτηρίαν, “to those who are eagerly waiting for him for salvation.” Three appearings, three words: He appeared once, φανερόω in verse 26; He appears now for us, ἐμφανίζω in verse 24; He will appear again, ὁράω here in verse 28.

visualMeditations.title: Behind the Curtain
visualMeditations.image: Picture the tabernacle in the wilderness. In the outer room, priests come and go all day: trimming lamps, burning incense, changing bread. Behind a thick, embroidered curtain lies the inner room, silent and dark except for the glory above the ark. No one enters — except one man, once a year, trembling, carrying blood. Everyone else waits outside. The curtain itself seems to say: ‘Not yet. The way is closed.’
visualMeditations.meaning: “but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood” (v. 7). “The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing” (v. 8). When Jesus died, “The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom” (Mark 15:38). Through Him, the way is open. You may come in.

visualMeditations.title: The Blood That Reaches the Conscience
visualMeditations.image: Picture someone scrubbing the outside of a cup until it gleams, while the inside remains stained and foul. Then picture a stream of clear, living water poured into the cup, flowing through every corner, dissolving every stain from within. The outside washing was not useless, but only the inner washing makes the cup truly clean.
visualMeditations.meaning: The old sacrifices could “sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh” (v. 13). “how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” (v. 14). Christ's blood reaches where nothing else can: the guilty conscience. Let Him wash you within, and then serve the living God with a clean heart.

visualMeditations.title: Three Appearings
visualMeditations.image: Picture three windows in a cathedral. The first shows a cross on a hill, with a Man dying under a darkened sky. The second shows a throne room in heaven, where the same Man, now risen, stands before the Father's face, pleading for His people. The third shows the sky splitting open and the same Man coming in glory, while crowds lift their faces in joy.
visualMeditations.meaning: He “has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself” (v. 26). He has entered “into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us” (v. 24). And He “will appear a second time, without sin, to those who are eagerly waiting for him for salvation” (v. 28). Three different Greek words, three appearings: past, present and future. Live between the cross and the return, with your High Priest appearing for you now.

structure.label: The Earthly Tabernacle (v. 1-10)
structure.body: The first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary: an outer room with the lampstand, table and bread of the Presence, and behind the second curtain the Most Holy Place with the golden incense altar and the ark containing manna, Aaron's staff and the tablets, beneath the cherubim over the mercy seat; priests served continually in the outer room, but only the high priest entered the inner room once a year with blood for himself and the people's unintentional sins, showing that the way into the holy place was not yet open; its gifts and sacrifices could not perfect the conscience but were external regulations until the time of reformation.

structure.label: Christ's Better Sacrifice (v. 11-14)
structure.body: Christ came as high priest of the good things to come, through a greater, more perfect tent not made with hands, and entered the holy place once for all by His own blood, obtaining eternal redemption; if animal blood and ashes cleansed the flesh, how much more will Christ's blood, offered through the eternal Spirit, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God.

structure.label: The Mediator's Death Puts the Covenant in Force (v. 15-22)
structure.body: Christ is mediator of a new covenant, since His death redeems transgressions under the first covenant so that the called may receive the eternal inheritance; as a will takes effect only after death, so the first covenant was inaugurated with blood, when Moses sprinkled the book, the people, the tabernacle and its vessels; under the law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

structure.label: Once for All, and Coming Again (v. 23-28)
structure.body: The heavenly realities needed better sacrifices than the copies; Christ entered not a man-made sanctuary but heaven itself to appear before God for us, not to offer Himself repeatedly as the high priest does each year, but once for all at the end of the ages to put away sin by His sacrifice; as people die once and then face judgement, so Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many and will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly wait for Him.

sections.heading: A Sanctuary That Preached a Sermon
paragraphs: Chapter 9 describes the tabernacle Moses built: an outer room, the Holy Place, with the lampstand, table and bread; and an inner room, the Holy of Holies, with the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat and the cherubim of glory. The priests went into the outer room every day. But “into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself, and for the errors of the people” (v. 7).

The writer sees a message in the layout: “The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing” (v. 8). The curtain said, ‘Keep out.’ The once-a-year entry said, ‘Access is restricted.’ The repeated sacrifices said, ‘The problem is not solved.’ The whole system was “a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect” (v. 9).

Two time-family words appear here. The ‘present age’ (v. 9) and the ‘time of reformation’ (v. 10) both use καιρός, a season with a particular character. Later, Christ appears ‘at the end of the ages’ (v. 26), using αἰών, the great eras of history. The old covenant was a season; it was “imposed until a time of reformation” (v. 10). With Christ, that time of setting things right has come.

sections.heading: How Much More the Blood of Christ
paragraphs: Then comes the contrast: “But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands” (v. 11), “nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption” (v. 12). The old high priest brought someone else's blood, entered an earthly tent, and had to return every year. Christ brought His own blood, entered heaven itself, and did it once for all.

The result is a cleansing the old system could never give: “how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” (v. 14). Animal blood could make a person ritually clean on the outside. Christ's blood reaches the conscience, the inner sense of guilt before God. John writes, “the blood of Jesus Christ, his Son, cleanses us from all sin” (1 John 1:7).

And this cleansing has a purpose: “to serve the living God” (v. 14). The servant-family word λατρεύω means to serve in worship. We are not cleansed merely to feel better, but to be free to worship and serve God with a clear conscience. Paul says, “in whom we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace” (Ephesians 1:7).

sections.heading: Once, Now and Again
paragraphs: Christ's death put the new covenant into effect. The writer plays on the word διαθήκη, which means both ‘covenant’ and ‘will’: “For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it” (v. 16). Even the old covenant began with blood, when Moses sprinkled the book and the people, saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you” (v. 20). The principle stands: “apart from shedding of blood there is no remission” (v. 22). Jesus said at the Last Supper, “for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins” (Matthew 26:28).

Verses 24–28 then describe three ‘appearings’ of Christ, each with a different word from the appear family. Past: “But now once at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself” (v. 26). Present: He has entered “into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us” (v. 24). Future: He “will appear a second time, without sin, to those who are eagerly waiting for him for salvation” (v. 28).

Between the first and third appearings comes the solemn reality of every human life: “Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment” (v. 27). There is one life and then judgement. But for those who belong to Christ, the judgement has already fallen on Him: He was “offered once to bear the sins of many” (v. 28). Jesus said that the one who believes “has eternal life, and doesn’t come into judgment, but has passed out of death into life” (John 5:24). Believers wait for His return not with dread but with eager longing.

ntConnection.heading: The Blood, the Torn Veil and the Return
paragraphs: The New Testament repeatedly celebrates the power of Christ's blood. We were redeemed “with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ” (1 Peter 1:19). God reconciled all things to Himself, “having made peace through the blood of his cross” (Colossians 1:20). And Christ is the one “who loves us, and washed us from our sins by his blood” (Revelation 1:5). John the Baptist pointed to Him: “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29).

At the moment Jesus died, the curtain that symbolised restricted access was torn: “The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom” (Mark 15:38). Luke adds, “The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two” (Luke 23:45). The torn veil announced what Hebrews 9:8 had anticipated: the way into the holy place is now open.

The promise of Christ's second appearing runs through the New Testament. The angels told the disciples, “This Jesus, who was received up from you into the sky, will come back in the same way as you saw him going into the sky” (Acts 1:11). Jesus promised, “I will come again, and will receive you to myself” (John 14:3). “For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout” (1 Thessalonians 4:16). And “when he is revealed, we will be like him; for we will see him just as he is” (1 John 3:2).

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple).” It was the golden cover of the ark where the high priest sprinkled blood on the Day of Atonement, between the cherubim, where God met His people. Paul uses the same word of Christ: God ‘sent to be an atoning sacrifice’ (Romans 3:25). Jesus is both the place where God meets sinners and the sacrifice that makes it possible.

Strong's: “a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage.” It literally means something ‘thrown alongside’ for comparison — the word for Jesus' parables. In Hebrews 9:9 the whole tabernacle system is a ‘parable’ of its time: a picture that teaches by comparison. This study tags it in the pattern family.

Strong's: “a ransoming (figuratively).” It describes release by payment of a price, as a slave or prisoner was freed. Zechariah and Anna used it of the redemption Israel longed for (Luke 1:68; 2:38). Christ obtained ‘eternal redemption’ by His own blood: the price was paid in full, and the freedom lasts forever.

Strong's: “an effusion of blood.” It may have been coined by the writer, combining αἷμα (blood) and ἐκχέω (to pour out). It sums up the whole sacrificial system: forgiveness requires a life poured out. The principle points to the cross, where Christ's blood was ‘poured out for many for the remission of sins’ (Matthew 26:28).

Strong's: “to expect fully.” It combines three parts — ἀπό, ἐκ and δέχομαι, to receive — and describes eager, intent waiting, like someone leaning forward to watch for an arrival. Paul uses it of creation and believers waiting for the redemption of the body, and of waiting for the Saviour from heaven. Christians are not just people who believe in the second coming; they eagerly await it.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit shows you the open way, the cleansing blood, and the coming King.

items.title: The Way Is Open
items.body: The Spirit once taught through a closed curtain that the way was not yet open. Now He testifies that the way is open through Christ's blood. Are you still living as if God's presence were off limits to you? Ask the Spirit to give you confidence to come close.

items.title: A Clean Conscience
items.body: Christ's blood cleanses the conscience from dead works. The Spirit wants to free you from guilt for confessed sin and from the deadness of religious performance. Bring to Him whatever still weighs on your conscience, and receive cleansing so you can serve the living God with joy.

items.title: Eagerly Waiting
items.body: Christ will appear a second time to bring salvation to those who eagerly wait for Him. The Spirit wants to stir in you a longing for Jesus' return. Ask Him to make that hope bright and to shape how you live now.

audit.title: The Access Check
audit.body: Do you approach God as if the curtain were still closed — distant, fearful, unsure of welcome? Meditate on verse 12 and draw near with confidence.

audit.title: The Conscience Check
audit.body: Is there anything on your conscience — confessed sin you still feel guilty for, or dead religious habits? Pray verse 14 over it specifically.

audit.title: The Readiness Check
audit.body: Verse 27 says everyone dies once and then faces judgement. Are you ready? Is there someone you need to talk to about this?

practices.title: Meditate on the Three Appearings
practices.body: For three days, take one ‘appearing’ each day: Christ revealed at the cross (v. 26), Christ appearing before God for you now (v. 24), and Christ appearing again (v. 28). Read the verse, thank Him for that aspect of His work, and write down how it changes the way you will live that day.

practices.title: Clean-Conscience Service
practices.body: Because Christ cleansed your conscience ‘to serve the living God’ (v. 14), choose one act of service this week offered as worship — not to earn God's favour but in gratitude for cleansing. Before you do it, pray, ‘Lord, I serve You freely because You have made me clean.’

prayerReflection: “Lord Jesus, thank You that You are the High Priest of the good things to come. The old tabernacle was a picture, with a curtain that said the way was not yet open. But You entered, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with Your own blood, once for all into the holy place, and You obtained eternal redemption. Through the eternal Spirit You offered Yourself without blemish to God. Cleanse my conscience from dead works, so that I may serve the living God. Thank You for being the mediator of a new covenant, sealed by Your death, so that I may receive the promised eternal inheritance. Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness, and You poured out Your blood for me. You appeared once at the end of the ages to put away sin by Your sacrifice. You appear now in God's presence for me. And You will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to bring salvation. I eagerly wait for You. In the mighty name of Jesus, Amen!”

storyConnections.title: The Day of Atonement
storyConnections.summary: Once a year, on the Day of Atonement, the high priest bathed, put on simple linen garments and offered a bull for his own sins. He took a censer of burning coals and incense into the Most Holy Place, so that the cloud would cover the mercy seat, and sprinkled the bull's blood on and before it. Then he killed a goat for the people's sins and did the same with its blood. A second goat, the scapegoat, had the people's sins confessed over it and was sent away into the wilderness. Hebrews 9 contrasts this yearly ritual with Christ, who entered heaven itself once for all with His own blood.

storyConnections.title: Moses Seals the Covenant With Blood
storyConnections.summary: After God gave the law at Sinai, Moses wrote down all the LORD's words and built an altar at the foot of the mountain. Young men offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Moses took half the blood and splashed it on the altar. Then he read the Book of the Covenant to the people, who promised to obey. Moses took the blood, sprinkled it on the people, and said it was the blood of the covenant the LORD had made with them. Hebrews 9:19–20 recalls this moment to show that covenants are inaugurated with blood — and that Christ's blood inaugurates the new covenant.

storyConnections.title: The Veil Torn at the Cross
storyConnections.summary: From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the land as Jesus hung on the cross. At three He cried out with a loud voice and breathed His last. At that moment, “The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom” (Mark 15:38) — torn from above, by God. The centurion who saw how Jesus died said, ‘Truly this man was the Son of God!’ Hebrews 9 explains what the torn veil means: the way into God's presence, closed while the first tabernacle stood, has been opened by Christ's death.
